# FlipLens: full text

Source: https://fliplens.eu. Updated 2026-10-12.


## How FlipLens works

URL: https://fliplens.eu/how-it-works

FlipLens answers one question: "I can buy this for €X. Is it worth buying to resell?" Here is exactly how the answer is made, including where it can be wrong.

### 1. Identify the exact product

You take a photo of the item or its label, scan the barcode on the box, or type the model. Photos are identified by an AI vision model; barcodes (EAN and UPC) are matched against marketplace listings. FlipLens looks for the details that change the price: model generation (WH-1000XM4 is not XM5), storage (128 GB is not 256 GB), lens mount (RF is not EF) and condition. You can correct anything before the check runs.

### 2. Find comparable listings

FlipLens searches current eBay listings through the official eBay API: in Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands, with prices converted to euro at European Central Bank rates, or on eBay.co.uk in pounds if you sell in the UK (the default there, selectable from any country). One tap on the result shows a UK vs EU comparison: the same item on eBay.co.uk and on the five EU sites side by side, in pounds and euros, without using a check. It then filters out what would distort the price: other models and variants, accessories sold on their own, bundles, broken or "for parts" items, duplicates and listings in a very different condition. You can see every listing that was used and why others were removed.

### 3. Estimate the resale value

From the remaining listings FlipLens builds a price distribution adjusted to your item's condition and reports three numbers: a quick-sale price, the expected sale price and a high asking price. Because asking prices are usually above final sale prices, the estimate is adjusted down. Every estimate carries a confidence score based on how many listings matched, how much they agree and how well the product was identified.

### 4. Calculate profit after fees

FlipLens subtracts the selling fees of the marketplace you sell on (for example eBay.de private or business, eBay.co.uk private, Vinted or local pickup), your shipping cost and the purchase price. The result is profit, return on investment (ROI) and the maximum price worth paying for your target ROI: max price = money you keep after fees and shipping ÷ (1 + target ROI).

### 5. Give a verdict, or say it does not know

The verdict is strong buy, buy, borderline or skip, with the reasons and risks behind it. If fewer than five matching listings remain, or the product identification is too uncertain, FlipLens says "not enough market data" instead of inventing a number.

### Known limits

- Prices are based on active listings (asking prices), not on confirmed sale prices.
- Supply is visible (how many items are for sale and for how long), sell-through speed is not yet.
- Collectibles and one-of-a-kind items are not supported. Clothes, shoes and bags are priced by brand, type and condition, not by the exact piece.
- Fees change: each fee profile shows when it was last checked and links to its source.

## Frequently asked questions

URL: https://fliplens.eu/faq

Short answers about how FlipLens works and what it can and cannot do.

**What is FlipLens?**
FlipLens is a web app for resellers in Europe. Take a photo, scan a barcode or type a model, and it tells you what the item resells for on eBay in Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands or on eBay.co.uk in the UK, your profit after fees and shipping, the most you should pay, and a verdict: strong buy, buy, borderline or skip.

**Where do the prices come from?**
From active eBay listings, read through the official eBay API: eBay in five EU countries in euro (converted with ECB exchange rates), or eBay.co.uk in pounds if you sell in the UK. Asking prices are usually above what items finally sell for, so FlipLens adjusts them down and always shows how many listings an estimate is based on. You can open every listing it used.

**Which items work best?**
Consumer electronics, gaming and cameras: headphones, smartphones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches, speakers, consoles, handhelds, controllers, games, camera bodies, lenses, action and compact cameras, plus power tools. Branded clothes, shoes and bags are priced too, by brand, type and condition (a rougher estimate than for electronics). LEGO sets by set number; books, vinyl, CDs and DVDs by barcode. Watches by model; branded jewellery by brand and type (unbranded gold and silver, furniture and vehicles are not priced).

**Do I need to enter a price?**
No. Without a price FlipLens shows what the item sells for and the maximum price worth paying for your target return. With a price you get a verdict, profit and ROI for that exact deal.

**What happens to my photos and data?**
Photos are only used to identify the item and are never stored. Your checks are kept until you delete them, and you can export or delete everything from your profile at any time.

**Is FlipLens affiliated with eBay?**
No. FlipLens is independent and shows eBay data through the official eBay API. It does not buy, sell or ship anything.

**Can FlipLens check a whole table at once?**
Yes. Take one photo of a stall, a box or a shelf and FlipLens finds up to 6 items, checks each against real eBay listings (one check per item) and lists the best buys first. Or keep the camera open with the live radar: items get a box with their name as you move, and a tap checks the price. Prices only ever come from a real check, never from a guess. Both need a Google sign-in.

**Which countries does FlipLens cover?**
The UK and five EU countries. If you sell on eBay.co.uk (the default when your country is the United Kingdom), FlipLens uses eBay.co.uk listings and shows prices in pounds, with UK private seller fees. Otherwise market data comes from eBay Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands, in euro. You can pick eBay.de or eBay.co.uk in your profile whatever your country, and the UK vs EU comparison on the result shows the same item on eBay.co.uk and on the five EU sites side by side, in pounds and euros, without using a check. Links to check prices yourself are available for Vinted, Kleinanzeigen and other marketplaces.

**How accurate is the estimate?**
It depends on the market. Every result shows a confidence score, how many listings it is based on and the risks. When there is not enough data, FlipLens says so instead of guessing. You can track your real sale prices in Stock and see how close the estimates were.

**Which marketplaces are the fees calculated for?**
eBay.de for private and business sellers, eBay.co.uk for private sellers, Vinted and local pickup with cash. Each fee profile shows when it was last checked.

**Can FlipLens write my listing?**
Yes. Take a photo of any item, clothes included, and FlipLens writes a title, description and condition text in the style of Vinted, eBay or Kleinanzeigen, in your language, ready to copy. Free includes 3 listings a month, Pro 100. FlipLens never posts on your behalf.

**Is there a mobile app?**
FlipLens is a web app that installs on your phone: open fliplens.eu and choose "Add to Home Screen" (iPhone) or "Install app" (Android). It then opens full screen like a native app.

**Is there a browser extension?**
Yes, for Chrome, Edge and Brave on a computer. On a listing on Vinted, Kleinanzeigen, eBay, Subito, leboncoin, Wallapop, Marktplaats, 2dehands or willhaben it shows a FlipLens panel: one click and you see what the item resells for, your profit after fees and the most to pay, with your app settings. It reads only the listing you open, and only after you click. Open fliplens.eu on your computer and choose "Add to Chrome", then sign in once in the app.

**Why do I need to sign in?**
Your free checks, history and plan belong to your account, so they work on all your devices. Sign in with Google in one tap; there is no password to create.


## How to check an item's resale value before you buy it

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/how-to-check-resale-value

At a flea market or on a classifieds site you usually have a minute to decide. This is the method resellers use, and the one FlipLens automates.

### 1. Pin down the exact model

Price differences between variants are often bigger than between conditions. Read the model number on the label, the box or the settings screen. Check storage size, model generation, colour where it matters, and for lenses the mount. "Sony headphones" is not a price; "Sony WH-1000XM4" is.

### 2. Look at comparable listings, not the first result

Search the exact model on eBay and filter out what does not compare: other generations, accessories sold alone, bundles with games or extra lenses, "for parts" items and listings from far away with expensive shipping. Look at several countries: the same item can sell for noticeably different prices in Germany, France or Italy.

### 3. Correct for asking price and condition

Most listings show asking prices, and items usually sell for less. Take the middle of the realistic range, not the highest listing, and adjust for condition: a "good" item does not fetch a "like new" price. If only a handful of comparable listings exist, treat any estimate with caution.

### 4. Subtract fees and shipping

What you keep is the sale price minus marketplace fees and the shipping you pay. On eBay.de private sellers pay no selling fees within Germany, business sellers do; on Vinted the buyer pays the fees. See eBay.de fees for private and business sellers (/guides/ebay-fees-germany) and where to sell used electronics in Europe (/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe).

### 5. Work out your maximum price

Decide the return you want, then divide what you keep by 1 plus that return. Example: a Nintendo Switch OLED expected to sell for €176, no selling fee, €6 shipping, so you keep €170. For a 40% return the most you should pay is €170 ÷ 1.4 = €121. Anything below is a buy; above it, negotiate or walk away.

### Do it in seconds with FlipLens

FlipLens does all five steps from a photo, a barcode or a typed model: it identifies the exact variant, reads comparable eBay listings in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk, adjusts for condition and asking prices, subtracts your marketplace fees and shipping, and shows the maximum price worth paying. You do not even need to know the seller's price.

**How do I know what something will resell for?**
Identify the exact model, compare it with similar listings in the same condition, take the realistic middle of the range rather than the top asking price, then subtract selling fees and shipping.

**How much should I pay for an item I want to resell?**
Divide what you will keep after fees and shipping by 1 plus your target return. For €170 kept and a 40% target, pay at most €121.


## eBay.de fees in 2026: private vs business sellers

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/ebay-fees-germany

Whether you sell as a private person or as a business changes your margin on every item. Here is the difference and how to account for it. Always confirm current fees on eBay's own pages before relying on them.

### Private sellers

Since 1 March 2023 private sellers on eBay.de pay no selling fees for sales within Germany. Optional extras, such as some listing upgrades and international selling, can still cost money. Source: eBay.de help: fees for private sellers (https://www.ebay.de/help/selling/fees-credits-invoices/gebhren-fr-private-verkufer-die-der-zahlungsabwicklung-teilnehmen?id=4822).

### Business sellers

Business sellers pay a final value fee that depends on the category and on whether the item is new or used. As of our last check (September 2026), the rates for the categories FlipLens covers were approximately:
ItemFee
 | Used or refurbished electronics | 5%
 | New electronics | 7%
 | Accessories | 12%
 | Tools | 13%
 | Per order over €10 | + €0.45

These figures come from a secondary source and categories have exceptions, so check eBay's current fee table for your category.

### Example: the same item, two seller types

A used Nintendo Switch OLED sells for €176 and you pay €6 shipping.
- Private seller: no selling fee, you keep €170. For a 40% return you can pay up to €121.
- Business seller: about 5% (€8.80) plus €0.45, you keep about €160.75. For a 40% return you can pay up to about €114.

A difference of a few euros per item adds up over a month of sourcing, so set your seller type correctly in FlipLens: every check then uses the right fees.

### Private or business: which am I?

If you buy items with the intention of reselling them regularly, tax and consumer law usually treat that as a business activity, even when you started casually. This is general information, not legal or tax advice: check the rules in your country or ask an accountant.

**Do private sellers pay fees on eBay.de?**
No selling fees for sales within Germany since 1 March 2023. Optional extras and international selling can cost money.

**What do business sellers pay on eBay.de?**
A final value fee by category and condition; as of September 2026 roughly 5% for used electronics and 7% for new, plus €0.45 per order over €10. Check eBay's current fee table.


## Where to sell used electronics in Europe

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe

The best marketplace depends on the item, how fast you want to sell and who pays the fees. A quick comparison for resellers in the EU.

### eBay: the widest reach

eBay has country sites across Europe (Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and more) and buyers who search by exact model. It suits items with a clear model number: consoles, phones, headphones, cameras and lenses. Private sellers in Germany pay no selling fees within Germany; business sellers pay a fee by category. See eBay.de fees (/guides/ebay-fees-germany).

### Vinted: no seller fees

On Vinted the seller pays no fee: the buyer pays a buyer protection fee and shipping on top. That makes your price look higher to the buyer, so items may need to be listed a little lower. It works well for small, easy-to-ship electronics and gaming.

### Kleinanzeigen: local in Germany

Kleinanzeigen is the big classifieds site in Germany. Basic listings for private sellers are free, many buyers prefer pickup, and buyers expect to negotiate, so start a bit above your target price. Good for bulky or heavy items where shipping would eat the margin.

### Local pickup and cash

No fees and no shipping, but a smaller audience and slower sales. Worth it for large items or when you already have a buyer.

### Compare before you buy

Set the marketplace you usually sell on in FlipLens and every check uses its fees and shipping rules. The result also links to Vinted, Kleinanzeigen and other marketplaces so you can see local prices yourself.

**Is it better to sell electronics on eBay or Vinted?**
eBay reaches more buyers who search by exact model and suits higher-value items; on Vinted the seller pays no fee because the buyer pays buyer protection, which works well for small items. Compare what you keep after fees and shipping.

**Who pays the fees on Vinted?**
The buyer. Vinted charges the buyer a buyer protection fee and shipping; the seller receives the listed price.


## Flea market reselling checklist

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/flea-market-reselling-checklist

Most bad buys are not overpriced, they are the wrong variant, incomplete or locked. Run through this before you hand over cash.

### Before you go

- Charge your phone and bring a power bank: you will be checking prices on the spot.
- Bring small notes and coins, sellers rarely have change early in the morning.
- Know your maximum price per item type, or check it with FlipLens in a few seconds.

### Identify the exact item

- Find the model number on the label, battery compartment or box. Take a photo of it.
- Check storage size, generation and for lenses the mount.
- Barcodes on boxes identify the exact variant fastest.

### Test what you can

- Does it power on? Ask for a socket or bring a power bank and cable.
- Screens: dead pixels, burn-in, cracks. Ports: wobbly charging ports are common.
- Controllers and Joy-Cons: check for stick drift.
- Cameras and lenses: look through the lens against light for haze, fungus and scratches; check the shutter fires.
- Phones and tablets: check battery health in settings if possible.

### Check it is not locked

Phones, tablets, laptops and smartwatches can be tied to the previous owner's account (for example Apple's Activation Lock). A locked device is worth a fraction of its price. Ask the seller to show it is signed out or reset in front of you.

### Completeness adds value

The original box, charger, cables, lens caps and manuals all help an item sell faster and for more. Missing chargers and proprietary cables cost you money to replace.

### Decide on the numbers

Compare the asking price with the maximum price worth paying after fees and shipping. If the seller is above it, negotiate down to it or walk away. See how to check resale value (/guides/how-to-check-resale-value).

**What should I check before buying used electronics to resell?**
The exact model and variant, that it powers on and works, screen and port condition, that it is not locked to someone else's account, what accessories are included, and that the price is below your maximum after fees and shipping.


## Vinted listing generator

URL: https://fliplens.eu/vinted-listing-generator

Take a photo of the item and get a title, description and hashtags ready to paste into Vinted. Works for clothes, shoes, bags, home, toys and tech, in your language.

### How it works

- Take one to three photos: front, back and the brand or size label work best.
- Pick the condition and add what photos cannot show, such as size, material or a small flaw.
- Copy the title and description, open Vinted and paste.

### What it writes

For Vinted: a short, natural title (brand, item and one key detail), a friendly and honest description, one sentence about the condition and a few relevant search words and hashtags. The same photo can also become an eBay listing (keyword-first title, structured description) or a Kleinanzeigen ad (direct, with the usual private-sale note).

### Honest by design

The writer describes only what is visible in your photos or written in your details. It does not invent a size, material, brand or measurements. When something buyers usually ask about is missing, such as the size or measurements, it tells you so you can add it before you post.

### What about the price?

FlipLens does not read Vinted data. After writing your listing it links to similar items on Vinted so you can compare prices in a tap. For electronics, games and cameras, FlipLens can also estimate the resale value (/how-it-works) from eBay listings in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk.

### Plans

Free: 3 listings a month. Pro (€9.99/month): 100 listings and 100 price checks. Reseller (€19.99/month): up to 1,000. See pricing (/pricing).

**Is the Vinted listing generator free?**
Yes, 3 listings a month are free after signing in with Google. Pro includes 100 a month.

**Which languages does it write in?**
English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Dutch, Polish, Slovenian, Croatian, Czech, Portuguese and Swedish.

**Does it post to Vinted for me?**
No. You copy the text and paste it into Vinted yourself. FlipLens is independent and not affiliated with Vinted.

**Are my photos stored?**
No. Photos are only used to write the listing and are not stored.


## How to sell on Vinted

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/how-to-sell-on-vinted

Vinted is the biggest second-hand marketplace for clothes in Europe and works for small electronics and home items too. Clear photos, an honest description and the right price do most of the work.

### Who pays the fees

Sellers pay no selling fee on Vinted. The buyer pays a Buyer Protection fee and the shipping on top of your price, so the total they see is higher than what you asked. Optional paid promotions, such as bumping an item, are available to sellers. Fees can differ by country and change over time, so check Vinted's help centre for the current rules.

### Photos that get clicks

- Use daylight and a plain background.
- Show the front, the back, the brand label and the size label.
- Photograph flaws close up: buyers trust sellers who show them.
- Your first photo is what people see in search, so make it the clearest one.

### Title and description

Start the title with the brand and the item, then one key detail such as size or colour: "Levi's 501 jeans W32 L32, dark blue". In the description give the size and, for clothes, measurements (for example chest and length), the material from the care label, how it fits and the condition, including any flaws. Add a few words people search for, such as the style or the occasion.

### Choose the condition honestly

Vinted asks you to choose a condition, from "New with tags" to "Satisfactory". Picking a better condition than the item has is a common cause of disputes and returns. If in doubt, choose the lower one and explain in the description.

### Pricing

Search Vinted for the same brand and item in a similar condition and price within that range. Many buyers send offers, so leave a little room. Bundle discounts encourage buyers to take several items in one parcel, which also saves you trips to the post office.

### Shipping

Pack items securely, ship within the time Vinted gives you and keep the proof of postage until the buyer has confirmed the order.

### Write listings faster

The FlipLens listing generator (/vinted-listing-generator) turns a photo into a Vinted title and description in your language and tells you what buyers will ask about, such as size or measurements.

**Do sellers pay fees on Vinted?**
No selling fee. The buyer pays a Buyer Protection fee and shipping on top of the price. Optional promotions cost extra.

**How do I write a good Vinted description?**
Give the brand, size and measurements, material, fit and an honest condition including flaws, plus a few words buyers search for.


## How to check resale value in Europe: apps and methods compared

URL: https://fliplens.eu/best-resale-value-apps

There is no single perfect source for second-hand prices. Each method below answers a slightly different question. Here is what each one is good at, where it falls short, and when to use it.

### At a glance

MethodSpeedDataSold or asking pricesCountriesCost
 | FlipLens | Seconds, from a photo, barcode or model name | Active eBay listings, filtered and adjusted for condition | Asking prices, adjusted down | Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Netherlands at once, or the UK | 10 free checks a month, paid plans for more
 | eBay "Sold items" filter | A few minutes per item | Completed sales on one eBay site | Sold prices | One country at a time | Free
 | Vinted, Kleinanzeigen searches | A few minutes | Current local listings | Asking prices | One marketplace and region | Free
 | Google Lens, then a marketplace search | Fast to identify, slow to price | Visual match, then your own search | Whatever you find | Any | Free
 | Trade-in and buyback sites | Instant offer | The buyer's own price list | An offer to buy from you | Varies | Free

### FlipLens

FlipLens identifies the exact model from a photo, barcode or typed name, reads comparable active eBay listings in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk, removes other variants, bundles and broken items, adjusts for condition and returns a resale range, your profit after fees and shipping and the most you should pay. Good for: fast buying decisions at flea markets and on classifieds, when you do not want to research every item by hand. Limits: it works from asking prices, not confirmed sale prices; it covers consumer electronics, gaming, cameras and power tools, not fashion; if there are too few comparable listings it says so instead of estimating. See how it works (/how-it-works).

### eBay search with the "Sold items" filter

On eBay you can filter a search to show items that actually sold. Better than FlipLens at: showing real final prices rather than asking prices. Drawbacks: you check one eBay site at a time, you have to read through the results yourself to remove other generations, bundles and broken items, and you still need to subtract fees and shipping to know your profit. Worth doing for expensive items before you commit.

### Searching Vinted or Kleinanzeigen

Searching the marketplace you plan to sell on shows the competition you will face. Good for: local pricing and items that sell mainly through classifieds. Drawbacks: you only see asking prices, and listings that sit unsold for weeks pull the picture up. FlipLens links to these searches from every result so you can compare in a tap.

### Google Lens to identify an unknown item

When you do not know what an item is, an image search can find the name or model. Good for: unusual items, vintage pieces and anything without a readable label. Drawbacks: it identifies, it does not price; you still need to search marketplaces and judge condition and variants yourself.

### Trade-in and buyback offers

Some shops and websites make an instant offer to buy your used phone, console or camera. Good for: selling quickly with no effort. Drawbacks: the offer is what the buyer is willing to pay to resell it themselves, so it is usually well below what you could get selling privately. It is a floor, not a resale value.

### When to use which

- Standing at a stall, seconds to decide: FlipLens.
- An expensive item before you buy: FlipLens first, then the eBay sold filter to confirm.
- Pricing your own listing: look at what is for sale on your marketplace right now.
- No idea what the item is: Google Lens first.
- You just want it gone: a trade-in offer, knowing it is the lowest number.

**What is the most accurate way to find resale value?**
Recent sold prices for the exact model in the same condition, adjusted for fees and shipping. eBay's sold filter shows them for one country at a time; FlipLens gives a fast estimate from active listings across five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk.

**Why are trade-in offers so low?**
The buyer has to resell the item and make a profit, so the offer is below the private resale price.

**Is there a free way to check resale value?**
Yes. Marketplace searches and the eBay sold filter are free, and FlipLens includes 10 free checks a month.


## How much is my console worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/how-much-is-my-console-worth

Gaming gear resells well, but two consoles that look the same can be worth very different amounts. These are the details that decide the price.

### What drives the price

- Exact model and revision: for example a standard model versus an OLED or Slim version, or a disc versus a digital edition. The model number on the bottom or back tells you.
- Storage: larger internal storage usually sells for more.
- Condition: scratches on screens, yellowed plastic, loud fans and controller stick drift all lower the price.
- Completeness: original box, controllers, dock, cables and power supply. A console without its power supply is harder to sell.
- Account and bans: a console still linked to someone else's account, or one banned from online services, is worth much less.

### Controllers and games

Controllers are checked for stick drift and worn buttons; official controllers sell better than third-party ones. For games, the edition matters (standard, collector's, region), and whether the case, manual and any codes are complete. Sealed games and complete-in-box retro games are their own market: compare like with like.

### Common mistakes

- Comparing your item with a bundle that includes extra games or controllers.
- Taking the highest asking price as the value.
- Forgetting shipping: consoles are heavy and bulky.
- Buying a handheld without testing the screen and buttons.

### Quick checklist

- Model number and storage noted.
- Powers on, reads discs (if it has a drive), controllers connect.
- Signed out of all accounts or factory reset.
- Power supply and cables included.
- Price compared with the same model in the same condition.

### Where to sell and how to check quickly

Consoles sell well on eBay and locally; see where to sell used electronics in Europe (/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe). To check a console in seconds, scan its barcode or type the model in FlipLens: it compares listings on eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk and shows the most you should pay. How it works (/how-it-works).

**How do I find out which console model I have?**
Look for the model number on the bottom or back of the console or in the system settings. It tells you the exact version and often the storage size.

**Does the original box matter?**
Yes. A complete console with box, controllers and cables usually sells faster and for more than the console alone.


## Resale value of used cameras and lenses

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/resale-value-cameras-lenses

Camera gear keeps its value better than most electronics, but a single problem such as fungus in a lens can make an item nearly worthless. Check these points before you pay.

### What drives the price of a camera body

- Exact model: generations of the same line differ a lot in value.
- Shutter count: how many photos the camera has taken. A high count lowers the value; many cameras let you read it from the files or the menu.
- Sensor and screen: scratches, dead pixels and dust that will not clean.
- Completeness: battery, charger, strap, caps and box.
- Region and language: some imported models have different menus or warranty terms.

### What drives the price of a lens

- Mount: the same focal length exists for different mounts (for example Canon RF and EF, Sony E/FE, Nikon Z and F). Compare only the same mount.
- Optical condition: fungus, haze, separation and deep scratches seriously reduce the value. Shine a light through the lens from the back.
- Mechanics: autofocus works, zoom and focus rings are smooth, aperture blades are clean and dry.
- Version: many lenses exist in several versions (for example with or without stabilisation).

### Common mistakes

- Comparing a lens with the same focal length but a different mount or version.
- Not testing autofocus on a body.
- Missing fungus because the lens was not checked against light.
- Ignoring the shutter count on a body that looks clean.

### Quick checklist

- Model, mount and version written down.
- Lens checked against light for fungus and haze.
- Body powers on, takes a photo, shutter count known if possible.
- Battery and charger included.

### Where to sell and how to check quickly

Cameras and lenses sell well on eBay across Europe; see where to sell used electronics in Europe (/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe). FlipLens reads the model and mount from a photo of the label or lens barrel and compares listings on eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk. How it works (/how-it-works).

**How do I check a used lens for fungus?**
Shine a bright light through the lens from the back and look for thread-like patterns, spots or a milky haze inside the glass.

**Does shutter count matter when reselling?**
Yes. Buyers compare it with the expected life of the shutter for that model, so a low count helps the price.


## Resale value of used headphones and earbuds

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/resale-value-headphones

Popular headphones resell quickly, but generations look alike and batteries wear out. These are the details buyers check.

### What drives the price

- Exact generation: models from the same line, such as Sony WH-1000XM4 and WH-1000XM5, or different AirPods generations, sell for different prices. Check the model number on the headband, case or in the settings.
- Battery: wireless headphones and earbuds lose capacity over time; noticeably short battery life lowers the value.
- Ear pads and tips: worn or flaking pads put buyers off, but can often be replaced.
- Completeness: case, cable, adapter and box.
- Authenticity: popular earbuds are often counterfeited; serial numbers and pairing behaviour help to tell.

### Hygiene and earbuds

Many buyers are cautious about used in-ear products. Clean them carefully, replace silicone tips if possible and say so in the listing. A single missing earbud or a missing charging case makes a set much harder to sell.

### Common mistakes

- Confusing two generations that look almost the same.
- Not testing noise cancelling, microphones and both sides.
- Buying earbuds that are still linked to someone else's account.

### Quick checklist

- Model number and generation confirmed.
- Both sides work, noise cancelling and microphone tested.
- Battery holds a charge.
- Case, cable and tips included.
- Removed from the previous owner's account.

### Where to sell and how to check quickly

Headphones sell well on eBay and Vinted; see where to sell used electronics in Europe (/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe). In FlipLens a photo of the label or the box barcode is enough to identify the generation and compare prices on eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk. How it works (/how-it-works).

**How do I tell headphone generations apart?**
Read the model number printed on the headband, case or box, or in the companion app or Bluetooth settings.

**Can I sell used earbuds?**
Yes, but clean them, replace the tips if you can and describe their condition honestly. Complete sets with the charging case sell best.


## Selling a used phone in Europe

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/sell-used-phone-europe

Phones are the most common second-hand electronics, and the easiest to get wrong. A locked phone or the wrong storage size can turn a good deal into a loss.

### What drives the price

- Exact model: standard, Plus, Pro and Max versions differ a lot in value.
- Storage: more storage sells for more. Check it in the settings, not just on the box.
- Battery health: many phones show the battery condition in the settings; a weak battery lowers the price.
- Condition: screen scratches or cracks, back glass, frame dents, camera lenses, buttons and ports.
- Completeness: box and cable help a little; the phone itself matters most.

### Account locks and carrier locks

A phone that is still linked to the previous owner's account (for example Apple's Activation Lock or a Google account after a reset) cannot be set up by a new owner and is worth only a fraction of the price. Make sure the seller removes the account and resets the phone in front of you. Also check whether the phone is locked to a mobile network: unlocked phones sell to more buyers.

### Common mistakes

- Buying a phone that is still signed in to an account.
- Comparing prices of a different storage size or version.
- Not checking for a replaced or non-original screen.
- Ignoring battery health.

### Quick checklist

- Model and storage confirmed in the settings.
- Signed out of all accounts and factory reset.
- Not locked to a network.
- Battery health checked.
- Screen, cameras, speakers, microphone and charging port tested.

### Where to sell and how to check quickly

Phones sell on eBay, classifieds and Vinted; see where to sell used electronics in Europe (/guides/where-to-sell-used-electronics-europe). FlipLens identifies the model from a photo or barcode, lets you set the storage, and compares listings on eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk. How it works (/how-it-works).

**What should I check before buying a used phone?**
That it is signed out of all accounts and reset, not locked to a network, has the storage you expect, a healthy battery, and a working screen, cameras and charging port.

**Does storage size change the resale value?**
Yes. The same model with more storage usually sells for more, so always compare the same storage size.


## How much are my clothes worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/resale-value-branded-clothes

Second-hand clothes sell every day on Vinted and eBay, but prices range from a couple of euros to well over a hundred. The brand on the label decides most of it, the rest comes down to a few details buyers always check.

### What drives the price

- Brand: the biggest factor by far. Premium and outdoor brands keep much more of their value than fast fashion.
- Item type: a winter jacket or a leather bag sells for more than a T-shirt from the same brand.
- Named lines and styles: well-known lines such as Levi's 501 jeans or The North Face Nuptse jackets price differently from the brand's basic items, so compare like with like.
- Condition: new with tags, new without tags, very good, good or satisfactory. Stains, pilling, holes and faded colours lower the price.
- Size: common sizes sell faster; very large and very small sizes usually take longer to find a buyer.
- Season: coats and boots sell best in autumn and winter, light dresses and shorts in spring and summer.
- Completeness: a removable hood, a belt or a bag's dust bag help the price.

### Fast fashion versus premium brands

Fast-fashion brands such as Zara, H&M, Bershka and Pull&Bear usually resell for a few euros up to around 15 to 20, even in good condition. Premium, designer and outdoor brands are worth much more, which is also why they are copied. For valuable pieces, keep the authenticity tags and the receipt if you have them, and photograph the labels clearly: buyers ask for them.

### Where to sell clothes

- Vinted: the main marketplace for clothes in Europe. In most countries sellers pay no selling fee; the buyer pays shipping and a Buyer Protection fee on top. See how to sell on Vinted (/guides/how-to-sell-on-vinted).
- eBay: private sellers in Germany and the UK pay no selling fees, but the seller usually pays shipping. Good for premium brands and buyers in other countries.
- Locally: classifieds and flea markets, with no shipping at all, but fewer buyers for each item.

### How FlipLens estimates clothing prices

Photograph the item and its brand label. FlipLens reads the brand and the type (women, men or kids), then compares listings of the same brand and type in the same eBay category, across eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk, and adjusts the asking prices down. By default it values clothes for Vinted, taking off typical shipping because the buyer pays it there, and shows eBay side by side. Items without a recognisable brand are not priced.
This is a rougher estimate than for electronics: FlipLens compares the brand and type, not the exact piece. Treat it as a guide to the price range, then check similar listings before you set your final price. See how to check resale value (/guides/how-to-check-resale-value).

### From photo to Vinted listing

Once you know the range, FlipLens can write the Vinted title and description from the same photo with the Vinted listing generator (/vinted-listing-generator). Add the measurements and any flaws, and it is ready to post.

**Which clothing brands resell best?**
Premium, designer and outdoor brands keep much more value than fast fashion. Fast-fashion items from brands like Zara or H&M usually sell for a few euros up to around 15 to 20.

**Can FlipLens price unbranded clothes?**
No. FlipLens compares listings of the same brand and type, so items without a recognisable brand are not priced.

**Should I sell clothes on Vinted or eBay?**
Vinted is usually the first choice for clothes because sellers pay no selling fee in most countries and the buyer pays shipping. eBay is worth comparing for premium brands. FlipLens shows both side by side.


## Sneaker resale value: how much are my trainers worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/sneaker-resale-value

Sneakers are among the easiest shoes to resell, but two pairs from the same brand can be worth very different amounts. The model, the size and the condition decide most of the price.

### What drives the price

- Brand and model: named models such as the Nike Air Force 1 or the Adidas Samba price differently from a brand's basic trainers. Always compare the same model.
- Size: popular sizes sell fastest, roughly EU 40 to 44 for men and EU 37 to 39 for women. Very small or very large sizes take longer.
- Condition: new with tags, new without tags, very good, good or satisfactory. Buyers look at creases, worn soles, yellowed midsoles and the inside lining.
- Box and extras: the original box and spare laces help, especially for sought-after models.

### Authenticity

Popular sneakers are often faked, so buyers are careful. Photograph the size label inside the shoe, the box label and any receipt you have. Clear, honest photos sell faster than a listing that leaves buyers guessing.

### Cleaning and photos

- Clean the uppers and soles and wash or replace the laces.
- Photograph both shoes from the side, the front, the back, the soles and the size label.
- Show wear and flaws close up.
- Use daylight and a plain background.

### Where to sell sneakers

- Vinted: no selling fee for sellers in most of Europe; the buyer pays shipping and Buyer Protection. See how to sell on Vinted (/guides/how-to-sell-on-vinted).
- eBay: private sellers in Germany and the UK pay no selling fees, but the seller usually pays shipping.
- Locally: classifieds and flea markets, where buyers can try them on.

### Check the price with FlipLens

Photograph the sneakers and the size label. FlipLens reads the brand and type, compares listings of the same brand and type in the same eBay category across eBay in five EU countries or on eBay.co.uk, adjusts asking prices down and by default values them for Vinted, with eBay shown side by side. It compares brand and type rather than the exact pair, so treat it as a rough range. Then it can write the listing from the same photo with the Vinted listing generator (/vinted-listing-generator). See also how to check resale value (/guides/how-to-check-resale-value).

**Which sneaker sizes sell fastest?**
Popular sizes, roughly EU 40 to 44 for men and EU 37 to 39 for women, usually sell fastest. Very small and very large sizes take longer.

**Does the original box matter for sneakers?**
Yes. The original box helps buyers trust the pair and usually helps the price, especially for sought-after models.

**How accurate is the FlipLens estimate for sneakers?**
It is a rough range. FlipLens compares listings of the same brand and type, not the exact model and size, so check similar listings before you set your final price.


## How much is my LEGO set worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/lego-set-value

LEGO keeps its value better than most toys, but two boxes of the same set can sell for very different amounts. The set number tells you exactly what you have; condition and completeness decide the price.

### Find the set number

Every LEGO set has a set number of 4 to 6 digits. You find it on the box, on the front of the instructions and in the LEGO catalogue. The set number identifies the exact set, so always compare listings of that number, not just the theme or the name.
No box and no instructions? Search the catalogue by theme and a few distinctive pieces or minifigures until you find the matching set.

### Condition and completeness

- New, sealed: factory sealed in the original box (in German listings often called OVP). Usually the highest price.
- New, opened: box opened, bags still sealed or unused.
- Used, complete: all pieces, the instructions and all minifigures.
- Used without box: complete set, but no box. Worth less than with the box.
- Incomplete: missing pieces, minifigures or instructions. Missing minifigures and instructions cut the value a lot.

To check completeness, look up the inventory for the set number and tick off the parts and minifigures. Say clearly in your listing what is included.

### Retired sets, current sets, bulk bricks and copies

- Retired sets: once LEGO stops selling a set, its value often rises, especially when it is sealed or complete.
- Current sets: still sold in shops, so your used set competes with retail discounts and sells for less than you might expect.
- Bulk bricks: loose mixed bricks sell by weight. This is a separate market from complete sets.
- Copies: compatible bricks from other makers, such as Lepin, or listings marked "compatible" are not LEGO and are worth far less. Look for the LEGO logo on the studs.

### Where to sell LEGO

- eBay: the widest audience for complete and sealed sets. Private sellers in Germany and the UK pay no selling fees, but the seller usually pays shipping.
- Locally: Kleinanzeigen, classifieds and flea markets, good for large sets and bulk bricks with no shipping.
- Vinted: works well for smaller kids' sets.
- BrickLink: a marketplace for single parts and minifigures, useful if you sell them separately.

### Check the price with FlipLens

Take a photo of the box or the instructions. FlipLens reads the set number and compares listings of that exact set, leaving out instructions-only listings, incomplete sets, copies and bundles. It searches eBay in five EU countries or eBay.co.uk, adjusts asking prices down and shows the most to pay if you are buying to resell.
Sorting a whole box of sets? Use the "many items at once" mode: one photo per set, prices for all of them and listings written. See how to check resale value (/guides/how-to-check-resale-value) and the flea market reselling checklist (/guides/flea-market-reselling-checklist).

**Where do I find the LEGO set number?**
The set number has 4 to 6 digits and is printed on the box, on the front of the instructions and in the LEGO catalogue. It identifies the exact set.

**How much do missing minifigures lower the value?**
A lot. Minifigures and instructions are what buyers check first, so a set without them sells for much less than a complete one. Check the inventory for the set number before you sell.

**Are compatible bricks like Lepin worth the same as LEGO?**
No. Copies and compatible bricks are not LEGO and sell for far less. FlipLens leaves copies out when it compares prices.


## Resale value of books, vinyl records, CDs and DVDs

URL: https://fliplens.eu/guides/resale-value-books-vinyl-dvds

Most books, CDs and DVDs resell for a few euros, but a few editions are worth much more. The barcode tells you exactly which edition you have, and that is where the price starts.

### The barcode identifies the edition

Books carry an ISBN, music and films an EAN barcode. Both identify the exact edition, not just the title. The same novel or album can exist in many editions at very different prices, so always compare the same barcode.

### Edition and format matter

- Books: first editions, signed copies and hardcovers are usually worth more than later printings and paperbacks.
- Vinyl: an original pressing is often worth more than a reissue. 180g pressings, coloured vinyl and picture discs have their own prices.
- Films: DVD, Blu-ray and 4K are different products. Steelbooks and complete box sets often sell for more.
- Condition: scratches, a worn sleeve, a damaged case, notes or underlining lower the price. Missing booklets or discs in a box set lower it a lot.

### What is actually worth selling

Mass-market books, CDs and DVDs usually resell for a few euros each. The value is in rare editions, popular vinyl and complete box sets. For cheap items, bundles sell well: a series of books, a stack of CDs by one artist or a set of films in one listing saves shipping and time.

### Buyback services or selling yourself

- Buyback services: such as Momox and reBuy in Germany or WeBuyBooks and Ziffit in the UK. You scan the barcode, get an offer and send the items in. They pay quickly, but the price is low.
- eBay and Vinted: selling yourself takes more effort, but usually brings more for valuable editions, vinyl and box sets.
- Locally: flea markets and classifieds, good for bundles and boxes of cheap items.

### Check the price with FlipLens

Scan the barcode or take a photo of the cover. FlipLens searches the exact edition by its barcode on eBay in five EU countries or eBay.co.uk, adjusts asking prices down and shows the most to pay if you are buying to resell.
For a box of books or a stack of records, use the "many items at once" mode: one photo per item, prices for all of them and listings written. See how to check resale value (/guides/how-to-check-resale-value) and the flea market reselling checklist (/guides/flea-market-reselling-checklist).

**Are my old books and DVDs worth anything?**
Most mass-market books, CDs and DVDs resell for a few euros. Rare editions, popular vinyl and complete box sets are worth more. Check the barcode to find the exact edition.

**Should I use a buyback service or sell myself?**
Buyback services pay quickly but low. Selling yourself on eBay or Vinted usually brings more for valuable items, while cheap items often sell best as bundles.

**Can FlipLens price a whole box of books or records?**
Yes. In "many items at once" mode you take one photo per item, and FlipLens prices all of them and writes the listings.


## About FlipLens

URL: https://fliplens.eu/about

FlipLens helps people who buy second-hand to resell decide in seconds whether an item is worth it, using real marketplace data from across Europe.

### What it is

A web app for resellers and bargain hunters. Take a photo, scan a barcode or type a model, and FlipLens shows the resale range, your profit after fees and shipping, the most you should pay and a clear verdict. It also writes listings for Vinted, eBay and Kleinanzeigen from a photo and tracks what you bought and sold.

### Who runs it

FlipLens is run by Evgenii Stepanishin in Slovenia. Contact: support@fliplens.eu (mailto:support@fliplens.eu). Creators and partners: see the partner programme (/partner).

### Where the data comes from

Prices come from active eBay listings, read through the official eBay API: in Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands, converted to euro with European Central Bank exchange rates, or on eBay.co.uk in pounds for sellers in the UK. Item recognition uses an AI vision model. Details and limits are explained in how it works (/how-it-works).

### Principles

- Photos are never stored. They are only used to identify the item or write the listing.
- No eBay data is stored. Listings are read live and cached briefly, as the eBay API licence requires.
- Honest about uncertainty. Every estimate shows its confidence; with too little data FlipLens says so instead of guessing.
- Independent. FlipLens is not affiliated with eBay, Vinted or Kleinanzeigen and does not buy, sell or ship items.

### Languages

FlipLens is available in English, German, Italian and French. The app follows your browser language; German pages are under fliplens.eu/de, Italian under fliplens.eu/it and French under fliplens.eu/fr. See also the Privacy Policy (/privacy) and Terms (/terms).

## How much is a used Nintendo Switch OLED worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/nintendo-switch-oled

The Switch OLED is one of the most traded consoles on eBay and Vinted. Since the Switch 2 came out in 2025 many more are for sale, so old price guides are out of date: compare current listings only.

### Which one do you have?

The OLED model has a 7-inch screen, a wide adjustable stand along the whole back and a dock with a LAN port. The model number on the back is HEG-001. The original Switch (HAC-001) and the Switch Lite (HDH-001) are different products with lower prices, so make sure listings you compare with are the OLED.

### What decides the price

- Edition: special editions (for example Zelda or Pokémon designs) usually sell above the white and neon versions, but only when the matching dock and Joy-Con are included.
- Joy-Con: stick drift is the most common fault and lowers the price. Original Joy-Con sell better than third-party ones.
- Screen: scratches on the OLED screen are hard to hide in photos and cost more than scratches on the back.
- Completeness: dock, power supply, HDMI cable, Joy-Con grip and straps, and the original box.
- Bundles: games and cases add less than their shop price. Compare a console alone with consoles alone.

### Check before you buy

- Joy-Con: move both sticks slowly in a circle in System Settings, Controllers and Sensors, Calibrate Control Sticks.
- Screen: look for scratches, dead pixels and lines on a white and a dark background.
- Dock: test TV output, the console should charge in the dock.
- Account: the seller should have removed their Nintendo Account and reset the console.
- Ask whether the console has been banned from online play.

### Where it sells best

Sells well on eBay and Vinted, and locally where buyers can test it. Ship in the original box or a padded box: the console and dock are fragile and heavy enough that shipping cost matters for your profit.

### Today's price

More used Switch OLED consoles came on the market after the Switch 2 launch in 2025, which pushed prices down. The OLED still sells steadily because it is cheaper and plays the same Switch games, so check the current price, not last year's.

**Is a Switch OLED without the box worth much less?**
Usually somewhat less, and it is harder to ship safely. The power supply and dock matter more than the box: a console without its dock is clearly worth less.


## How much is a used Nintendo Switch 2 worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/nintendo-switch-2

The Switch 2 launched in June 2025 and is still current, so used ones trade close to the new price. Small details, such as whether a game code was used, change what it is worth.

### Which one do you have?

The Switch 2 is larger than the original Switch, with a 7.9-inch screen and Joy-Con 2 controllers that attach with magnets. It came alone and in bundles with a game. Check whether a listing includes the game on a cartridge, as an unused download code, or not at all.

### What decides the price

- Bundle: a console with an unused game code is worth more than one where the code was redeemed. A used code adds nothing.
- Condition: as a current console, buyers expect it to look nearly new. Scratches and missing parts cost more than on older consoles.
- Completeness: dock, Joy-Con 2, grip, straps, power supply, cable and box.
- Region: a Japan-only version sold in Japan is limited to Japanese language and Japanese accounts. Check before buying an import.

### Check before you buy

- Ask for the receipt: it proves the console is not stolen and may still be under warranty.
- Test both Joy-Con 2 for drift and check the magnets hold firmly.
- The seller should remove their Nintendo Account and reset the console.
- If a game code is included, make sure it has not been redeemed.

### Where it sells best

Sells fast on eBay and Vinted. Because it is current, buyers compare with shop prices: a used console only sells well clearly below the new price.

### Today's price

Prices for a used Nintendo Switch 2 change every week, so this page gives no fixed numbers. Only rarely, in short periods when it is out of stock. Most of the time a used Switch 2 sells below the shop price, so resale profit comes from buying cheap, not from scarcity.

Only if it has not been redeemed. Ask the seller to show the unused code card or the email.


## How much is a used Nintendo Switch Lite worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/nintendo-switch-lite

The Switch Lite is cheap to buy and easy to ship, which makes it a popular flip. The catch is that its controllers are built in, so one fault affects the whole console.

### Which one do you have?

The Switch Lite (model HDH-001) is handheld only: no detachable Joy-Con and no TV output. It comes in several colours and some special editions. It is a different product from the Switch and Switch OLED, with a lower price.

### What decides the price

- Stick drift: the sticks cannot be swapped like Joy-Con, so drift lowers the price a lot.
- Screen: scratches and pressure marks.
- Colour and edition: special editions can sell for more than the standard colours.
- Charger: many are sold without one. It is cheap to replace, but buyers still pay less.

### Check before you buy

- Calibrate both sticks in System Settings and watch for movement when you let go.
- Press every button, including the D-pad and shoulder buttons.
- Check the battery: charge it and play for a few minutes.
- The seller should remove their Nintendo Account.

### Where it sells best

Small and light, so shipping is cheap. Sells well on Vinted and eBay, often with a game or a case. Price the console on its own first, then decide if the extras are worth listing separately.

## How much is a used PlayStation 5 worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/playstation-5

There are three PS5 generations, each with and without a disc drive. They look similar in photos but sell for clearly different prices, so knowing the exact model is the most important step.

### Which one do you have?

The model number on the back or the bottom starts with CFI. CFI-10xx and CFI-11xx are the original PS5 (825 GB). CFI-20xx is the PS5 Slim (1 TB) from 2023. CFI-70xx is the PS5 Pro (2 TB) from 2024, which has no disc drive. The Digital Edition has no disc drive; the Slim Digital Edition can get one as an add-on.

### What decides the price

- Model: Pro, Slim and original are three different price levels. Compare only with the same one.
- Disc drive: the disc version usually sells above the Digital Edition. A Slim Digital with the add-on drive sits in between.
- Controller: a DualSense with drift or worn sticks lowers the price.
- Condition: scratches on the glossy parts, yellowing of the white panels, fan noise.
- Bundles: games add less than their shop price. Value the console alone first.

### Check before you buy

- Read the model number (CFI-...) and the storage in Settings, System, System Software.
- Start a game: listen for loud fan noise and watch for crashes.
- Disc version: insert a disc and check it reads and ejects.
- The seller should sign out of PlayStation Network and reset the console.
- Test the controller for drift and check all buttons and triggers.

### Where it sells best

Sells well on eBay and locally. It is heavy, so ship in a sturdy box and include the shipping cost in your price. Local pickup avoids shipping damage and lets the buyer test it.

### Today's price

Prices for a used PlayStation 5 change every week, so this page gives no fixed numbers. FlipLens reads current eBay listings for the exact model and condition, removes bundles, broken items and other models, and shows a quick-sale, expected and high price, your profit after fees and the most to pay. URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/xbox-series-x

The Xbox Series X is a steady seller, but it is easy to mix up with the cheaper Series S. Here is what decides the price.

### Which one do you have?

The Series X is a tall black box with a disc drive (1 TB). Since 2024 there is also an all-digital white version and a 2 TB edition. The Xbox Series S is much smaller, mostly white, has no disc drive and sells for considerably less.

### What decides the price

- Version: disc, digital or 2 TB edition.
- Controller: included, working, no drift.
- Condition: scratches, dust in the vents, fan noise.

The Steam Deck has two generations and several storage sizes. The difference between them is bigger than most listings make clear.

### Which one do you have?

The LCD model (2022) came with 64 GB, 256 GB or 512 GB. The OLED model (2023) has a larger, brighter screen and comes with 512 GB or 1 TB. The storage is shown in Settings, System. The OLED is worth noticeably more than the LCD.

- Sticks and screen: drift, scratches and dead pixels.

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/airpods-pro-2

AirPods Pro 2 resell well but are among the most faked products on second-hand marketplaces. Checking authenticity is the first step.

There are two versions of the AirPods Pro 2: with a Lightning case (2022) and with a USB-C case (2023). The AirPods Pro 3 followed in 2025. Connected to an iPhone, Settings shows the exact model and serial number, which you can check on Apple's coverage site.

### What decides the price

- Authenticity: fakes are common. A genuine pair shows the correct serial in Settings and on Apple's coverage check.
- Battery: battery wear lowers the price.
- Case: USB-C or Lightning, scratches, the speaker and lanyard loop.

Tiny and cheap to ship, sells on eBay and Vinted. Buyers worry about fakes, so show the serial number check and the original box.

## How much is a used iPhone 13 worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/iphone-13

The iPhone 13 is a popular used phone in Europe. Storage, battery health and the parts history make the biggest difference to what it sells for.

### Which one do you have?

Settings, General, About shows the model, storage and serial. Make sure to compare with the same model: iPhone 13, 13 mini, 13 Pro and 13 Pro Max are four phones with very different prices.

### What decides the price

- Model and storage: 128 GB is the most common, larger storage sells for more.
- Battery health: shown in Settings, Battery. Low battery health lowers the price.
- Replaced parts: Settings, General, About shows "Parts and service history". A non-genuine screen or battery lowers the price.
- Condition: screen and frame scratches, cracked back glass.
- Locks: an iPhone with Activation Lock or a carrier lock is worth much less.

### Check before you buy

- Find My iPhone must be off and the phone reset to factory settings.
- Check battery health and parts history.
- Test Face ID, cameras, speakers and charging.
- Insert your SIM card to check it is not carrier locked.

### Where it sells best

Sells well on eBay and local marketplaces; buyers want photos of the battery health screen. Trade-in offers are faster but usually lower than selling yourself.

The MacBook Air M1 (2020) is still one of the most sought-after used laptops. In Europe one detail often gets overlooked: the keyboard layout.

The Apple menu, About This Mac shows the chip, memory and serial. The M1 Air has no fan, two USB-C ports and a wedge shape. The M2 Air (2022) is flat, has MagSafe and sells for more.

### What decides the price

- Battery: the cycle count is shown in System Information, Power.
- Keyboard layout: a German QWERTZ or French AZERTY keyboard limits buyers in other countries. Sell where the layout is local.
- Condition: dents, screen coating wear, keyboard shine.

- Check memory, storage and battery cycles.
- Test every key, the trackpad, the camera and both ports.
- Look for marks on the screen from the keyboard.

### Where it sells best

Sells well on eBay and local marketplaces. Sell in the country that matches the keyboard layout to reach the most buyers.

The Fujifilm X100V became famous on social media and is one of the few cameras whose used price stayed high for years. That also makes it a target for scams.

**Why is the X100V so expensive used?**
Demand from social media and limited supply kept prices high. Prices have moved since the X100VI launch, so check the current market.

**Does the X100VI lower the value of the X100V?**
A new model usually lowers the price of the previous one, but demand for the X100V has stayed strong.


## How much is a used Sony A7 III worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/sony-a7-iii

The Sony A7 III is a classic first full-frame camera and sells steadily. Shutter count and sensor condition matter most.

### Which one do you have?

The A7 III (ILCE-7M3) is often listed next to the A7 II, A7 IV and A7R models. The model code is on the bottom. Body only and kits with a lens are different products: compare like with like.

### What decides the price

- Shutter count: a high count lowers the price.
- Sensor and mount: scratches on the sensor or a worn mount.
- Kit: body only versus with a lens; value the lens separately.
- Accessories: batteries, charger, strap, box.

### Check before you buy

- Ask for the shutter count or read it from an image file with an online tool.
- Look at the sensor with the lens off and take a photo of a white wall at a small aperture.
- Test autofocus, stabilisation, card slots and screen.

### Where it sells best

Sells on eBay and camera marketplaces. Sell the body and lens separately if the lens is in demand on its own.

## How much is a used Levi's 501 jeans worth?

URL: https://fliplens.eu/resale-value/levis-501

Most used Levi's 501s are worth little, but some vintage pairs sell for a lot. The tags tell you which one you have.

### Which one do you have?

Look at the red tab, the care tag and the button. A capital "E" on the red tab ("Big E") marks pairs from before the early 1970s, which are collectible. Pairs made in the USA are generally more sought after than recent ones. The waist and length are on the leather or paper patch at the back.

### What decides the price

- Age and origin: vintage, Big E and Made in USA pairs above recent ones.
- Size: common sizes sell faster; vintage sizes run smaller than labelled.
- Fades and wear: natural fades are valued, but holes in the crotch lower the price.
- Fit: 501 versus other cuts such as 505 or 550.

### Check before you buy

- Read the red tab, care tag, button and patch.
- Measure the waist and length flat.
- Check the crotch and pockets for holes.

### Where it sells best

Recent 501s sell on Vinted for small amounts. Vintage pairs sell on eBay and vintage marketplaces: put "vintage", the decade and the origin in the title.

The North Face Nuptse puffer sells all winter, and prices rise when it gets cold. Fakes are common, so check before you buy.

Dr. Martens 1460 boots are an evergreen seller. Boots made in England and special editions sell for more than standard pairs.

### Which one do you have?

The 1460 is the classic 8-eye boot. The size is inside the boot and on the sole. The "Made in England" line is made in the original factory; standard pairs are made elsewhere.

### What decides the price

- Line: Made in England and special editions above standard.
- Wear: the soles and heels, creasing, scuffed toes.
- Size: common sizes sell fastest.
- Colour and leather: black smooth leather is the most common.

### Check before you buy

- Look at the soles: heavy heel wear lowers the price.
- Check the stitching and the yellow welt.
- Read the size and origin inside.

### Where it sells best

Sells on Vinted and eBay all year. Clean and polish before photographing.

### Today's price

Prices for a used Dr. Martens 1460 boots change every week, so this page gives no fixed numbers. **How much is a used Dr. Martens 1460 boots worth?**
It depends on line, size, wear and origin. Prices change weekly, so check today's value: type "Dr. Martens 1460 boots" and the condition into FlipLens (fliplens.eu), which compares current eBay listings in the UK and five EU countries and shows the expected sale price and the most worth paying.

**Are used Dr. Martens worth anything?**
Yes, they sell steadily. Good condition and Made in England pairs sell best.

**Does polishing make a difference?**
Yes, clean polished boots look better in photos and sell faster.
